title: fix(sqlite): report reader work and bound workspace sweep allocation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow cron hydration warnings can report zero statements even while SQLite performs substantial reads. Workspace maintenance also repeatedly copies its entire pending graph frontier when selecting each 256-node batch.

Related: #191711, #190295, #190938.

## User Impact

Read-only agent diagnostics now attribute native execution, including iterators and cached queries. Workspace sweeps allocate less memory while preserving their candidates and coherent snapshot. This does not claim to reduce historical transcript or workspace database I/O; those remaining scans are documented below. No schema, index, config, cache, retention, or permission change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ordinary read-only SQLite opener bypassed the engine opener's existing observation wrapper. Install that wrapper before statement caching. The prior hydration benchmark explicitly wrapped its own handle and therefore missed the production wiring defect; it now uses the actual read-only owner.

For sweeps, collect only the next batch from the pending Set instead of spreading the entire Set and slicing it. Traversal order, reachability, epoch checks, and query batches remain unchanged.

Production delta is +8 lines: two connect existing diagnostics, six replace unbounded transient copying with bounded collection. Tests grow by 53 lines, with a scoped allocation record: one real read-only attribution regression and wider coverage in the existing GC retention test. Existing benchmark scripts gain production-shaped payloads, native pager measurement, and a sweep workload.

## Evidence

The read-only regression fails on the base with `statementTiming.count: 0`, then passes with four native/cached statements and four rows across repeated snapshots. The actual hydration benchmark's positive-count proof also fails on the base and passes with 12 statements. All 36 reader/diagnostic tests and 39 workspace owner/sibling tests pass.

Synthetic-only measurements use five interleaved before/after pairs with A/A controls, separate allocation passes and CPU profiles. No production data is used. Local timing runs use macOS/APFS and Node 26.12.1. V8 allocation excludes native SQLite memory.

| Owner workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sweep, 3.21 GB shared DB: wall median | 1,102.3 ms | 1,044.2 ms |
| Sweep: CPU median | 1,170.6 ms | 1,117.0 ms |
| Sweep: sampled allocation | 308,004,992 B | 215,594,024 B |
| Sweep: native logical pager reads | 3,807,997,952 B | 3,807,997,952 B |
| Cron, 6.14 GB agent DB, 50k background events: wall median/p95 | 297.97 / 351.99 ms | 297.17 / 308.08 ms |
| Cron: thread CPU median | 291.03 ms | 290.36 ms |
| Cron: sampled allocation | 42,809,024 B | 47,393,524 B |
| Cron: native logical pager reads | 169,918,464 B | 169,918,464 B |

Enabling native timing has a real +10.7% sampled-allocation cost in the background-heavy case; wall/CPU remain within A/A variation. The sweep removes about 30% of sampled allocation. Its warm wall p95 is 1,391.9 ms versus baseline A1/A2 1,256.4/1,366.3 ms, so no tail-latency improvement is claimed. An uncontrolled first sweep pair is retained separately from the five warm pairs. All result digests and candidates match.

Reproduction owners: `scripts/perf/cron-hydration-statement-measure.ts` and `scripts/perf/local-workspace-manifest-read.ts --sweep` (see their header commands). Pager counts come from `SQLITE_DBSTATUS_CACHE_MISS` on the actual native connection, with mmap disabled and a 2 MiB page cache; they are distinct from Linux physical disk counters.

The excluded-user cron control reads 287,301,632 logical bytes for 50k events although dependency discovery returns zero candidates. In the background-result shape, dependency and TTL-prefix scans account for 99.66% of reads, while selected payload acquisition is only 184,320 bytes. A generic history cutoff would lose pending background results across compaction. No speculative cutoff or schema change is included.

Independent Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean on the complete local candidate against `3e3911e1d6d391f4d84cb2103a6031fb8fe32214`. Subsequent changes are mechanical script lint corrections only. `pnpm check:changed --base 3e3911e1d6d391f4d84cb2103a6031fb8fe32214` passes. Initial benchmark type/lint errors were repaired. An additional test-line ratchet reports six inherited lines over the ceiling on the pinned base: #190939 (`f2084811c1d1`) added 44 lines without allocation and exhausted 34 lines of slack; #191689 and #191732 subsequently removed two lines each. This is an existing main regression. Current main still has five lines of debt, so routine integration would not fix it. This PR allocates exactly its own 53 added test lines; no unrelated budget increase or test deletion is included. Reader tests took 6.24 s of test execution (37.14 s including build); workspace tests took 96.24 s wall, mostly transform/setup (39 passing). Linux Docker corroboration on Node 26.12.1 uses five alternating pairs and A/A controls: cron physical-read medians remain 117,567,488 B (background), 8,847,360 B (ordinary), and 289,128,448 B (excluded); sweep median remains 3,210,719,232 B. All results match. Cold-read ranges are retained separately; these virtual-block-storage counters do not establish production hardware latency.
